title: Community, Lemi Orhan Ergin
description: Software Craftsmanship Turkey, Agile Turkey, and the manifestos Lemi Orhan Ergin translated into Turkish.

blocks.text: Communities I have built or helped run, and manifestos I have translated into Turkish.

items.title: Software Craftsmanship Turkey
items.text: A community for developers who care about their craft. More than 200 free meetups so far, and code retreats, including the Global Day of Coderetreat, which I have facilitated since 2013. In 2015 it ran CraftSummit, the first software craftsmanship conference in Türkiye.

items.title: Agile Turkey
items.text: Ran its two meetup.com groups, Agile Buluşmalar and Agile Talks. Product owner and organization lead of Agile Turkey Summit 2015 and 2016.

items.title: Translations
items.text: Part of the team that translated the [Agile Manifesto](https://agilemanifesto.org/iso/tr/manifesto.html). Turkish translator of the [Software Craftsmanship Manifesto](https://manifesto.softwarecraftsmanship.org/#/tr), the [SOA Manifesto](http://www.soa-manifesto.org/default_turkish.html) and the Disciplined Agile Manifesto. One of the translators of the Nexus Guide, Scrum.org's guide to scaling Scrum, in 2016.

sections.heading: SCTurkey
blocks: I founded Software Craftsmanship Turkey (SCTurkey) on 7 March 2014, the fifth birthday of the Manifesto for Software Craftsmanship, as a non-profit, open community.[^1] By September 2016 [Erkan Erol](https://www.linkedin.com/in/erkanerol/) was organizing it with me,[^2] and by April 2019 [Aykut Bulgu](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mabulgu/) was too.[^3] Kommunity lists the three of us as its organizers today.[^4] The meetups ran on meetup.com from 2015 and moved to Kommunity in 2019. Kommunity also holds the meetup.com events, so the numbers below count the meetups that have an event page there.[^4][^5]

items.label: Event pages
items.text: 62 meetups held with an event page, 2015 – 2021[^4]

items.label: Rhythm
items.text: Wednesday evenings, mostly two weeks apart: 47 of the 52 meetups in 2017 – 2019 were on a Wednesday[^4]

items.label: Formats
items.text: Talks, coding dojos and TDD katas, a Clean Code reading group, a panel, and the Global Day of Coderetreat every November from 2017 to 2019[^4]

items.label: RSVPs
items.text: 130 for a typical meetup (the median), 244 at most in person and 1,142 online; these are RSVPs, not head counts[^4]

items.label: Members
items.text: 4,092 on Kommunity in November 2026;[^4] 5,098 on meetup.com in October 2019[^5]

blocks: SCTurkey ran CraftSummit 2015, the first software craftsmanship conference in Türkiye.[^6] There has not been another one since. I was its product owner and organization lead. ACM, the company where I was a managing partner, was the organizing company.[^6]

items.label: When
items.text: 30 May 2015, a one-day summit[^6]

items.label: Where
items.text: Bahçeşehir University, Fazıl Say Conference Room, Beşiktaş, Istanbul[^6]

items.label: Talks
items.text: Sandro Mancuso, Alexandru Bolboaca and Alvaro Garcia in English; Özcan Acar, Armağan Amcalar and I in Turkish; J. B. Rainsberger on video[^6]

items.label: My talk
items.text: [Unleashed Power Behind The Myths: Pair Programming](https://speakerdeck.com/lemiorhan/unleashed-power-behind-the-myths-pair-programming), in Turkish, the last session of the day; it is on the [Talks page](../talks/) too[^6]

sections.heading: Agile Turkey
blocks: Agile Turkey started Agile Buluşmalar in 2012 and held it every month: not a seminar but a conversation around a table, led by one person, with no slides.[^7] In 2015 and 2016 I ran its two meetup.com groups: Agile Buluşmalar in the evenings, and Agile Talks mostly in the afternoon.[^8][^9]

items.label: Agile Buluşmalar
items.text: 30 on the group's past-meetups counter: 15 in 2015 and 15 in 2016, at least one of them cancelled[^8][^10]

items.label: Agile Talks
items.text: 7 meetups: 6 in 2015 and 1 in 2016[^9]

items.label: Rhythm
items.text: Agile Buluşmalar on Tuesdays at 19:30; in the first half of 2016 mostly every two weeks, at İTÜ ARI Teknokent[^8][^11]

items.label: October 2015
items.text: 8 meetups in four days, 5 – 8 October, most of them The Agile Week of Agile Turkey Summit 2015[^7][^9][^12]

items.label: Guests
items.text: Paul Ellarby online in August 2015;[^9] Michael Feathers in October and Dave Farley in December 2015, both with Istanbul Coders[^7][^8]

items.label: Members
items.text: 1,422 in Agile Buluşmalar in July 2016;[^11] 930 in Agile Talks in November 2016[^9]

blocks: I was the product owner of Agile Turkey Summit for two years, 2015 and 2016. The 2016 summit's page names me as Agile Turkey's community lead and the summit's product owner.[^13] The summit had started in 2013, and 2016 was its fourth year.[^13]

items.text: 9 October, at Grand Cevahir Convention Center, Şişli, inside The Agile Week of trainings, workshops and meetups, 5 – 11 October.[^14] More than 600 people from 113 companies, 3 keynotes and 4 parallel tracks.[^13] Michael Feathers, Jurgen Appelo, Ahmed Sidky and Jonathan Rasmusson were among the speakers[^14]

6 October, at Wyndham Grand Levent, Şişli. The theme was “End to End Agile Mind Shift”, in four parallel tracks: DevOps, Agile in a Nutshell, The Mind Shift and Software Craftsmanship. Arie van Bennekum, a co-author of the Agile Manifesto, and Dave Farley were among the speakers, and the tickets sold out[^13]
